rationale: This is not a passing 20-option portfolio because the contact sheet currently shows only 9 options and only about 6 materially different spatial families. The set is over-concentrated in block/slab derivatives with repeated courtyard/notch/void logic, so the dominant family share is too high and the roof language repeats as prismatic, curved, or stepped variants without enough sectional divergence. The strongest program-aligned moves are the entry notch, lifted threshold, and stepped public terrace conditions, because they support an active street edge and a clear public void while keeping the upper mass calm. To become portfolio-grade, the next graph author should generate more distinct mass relations—especially split-wing, bent-bar, bridge, carve_void, and true courtyard-through forms—so the portfolio reads as a family of related but non-redundant neighborhood-building section types.
required_next_relations: Add at least one courtyard-threshold family with a true through-void, not just a shallow notch.
Add one bent-bar or split-wing massing where the public void is formed by separation between volumes.
Add one lifted base / bridged upper mass that clearly protects an active ground edge.
Add one carve_void or puncture family with a readable section change, not a roof-only edit.
Add one cross_mass or attach_volume option that changes access and public-space relation in plan and section.
Reduce the dependence on block-and-slab derivatives; each new card should alter both footprint and section.
Keep upper mass calm, but make the ground condition more varied: terrace, cut corner, inset court, and lifted edge should each read differently.
